findings.title: Safe render-model schema accepts unsafe nested token trees
findings.observation: Recursive inline children and Markdown list items use Type.Unknown(), so the advertised safe render DTO does not enforce the compiler's closed token model.
findings.trigger: A stored/legacy render model or a producer relying on the public schema supplies an unsafe nested link or unknown token below an otherwise valid outer node.
findings.impact: Response validation and OpenAPI accept values outside the safe model, and malformed persisted content can reach recursive renderer paths that assume constrained discriminants and HTTPS links.

evidence.description: The compiled schema returned true for strong.children containing a javascript: link whose child is an unknown html token.
The Web recursively consumes token.children and applies token.href without a second validator.

findings.remediation: Replace unknown recursive children/list items with recursively closed token/block schemas, regenerate OpenAPI and add negative nested-shape contract tests.
findings.verification: The unsafe nested counterexample is rejected, valid nested Markdown remains accepted and all contract/Web/full checks pass.

findings.title: Delivered rollback procedure contradicts the approved plan
findings.observation: The approved plan promises that the prior LP-02 binary runs against the additive LP-03 schema, but the delivered record confirms that binary rejects the additional migration row and substitutes forward-fix or backup restore.
findings.trigger: Migration 0003 is applied and the application is rolled back to the authoritative LP-02 binary without a schema rollback.
findings.impact: The old binary returns MIGRATION_MISMATCH, stays not-ready and cannot serve the old API behavior promised as the incident recovery path.

evidence.description: Implementation plan lines 477-478 require the LP-02 binary to run after application rollback.
The exact LP-02 readiness code returns MIGRATION_MISMATCH when ledger row count differs from its exact expected catalog.
The PR's verification record explicitly acknowledges this incompatibility and changes the recovery model.

findings.remediation: Either make the approved old-binary/additive-schema rollback executable and tested, or route and pass a revised technical plan that authorizes and verifies the different forward-fix/backup recovery model.
findings.verification: An executable recovery drill proves the approved behavior, or a newly approved exact plan and matching test replace it without contradictory documentation.
